walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.
To make the function run faster.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Because the syntax requires it.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
To make the function run faster.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
